items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: And I remember one that was named Silas Green from New Orleans. Yeah, yeah, I remember that. He was no relative of mine.

ctx.x: Well, there's so much talent here that it's very, very hard for jazz musicians to work like, well, in other towns. Yeah. Other towns, there's so few jazz musicians compared to New Orleans. Gentlemen, we have to pause for this break. In the meantime, I'll remind our audience that the number to call and talk it over with Mr. Johnny Wiggs of Johnny Wiggs and the New Orleans Kings. And Mr. Dick Allen is 523-2404. Give us a call. Let's talk it over. Say, be with me tonight on Mid-Month in New Orleans from 10. Mr. Dick…

Good morning, Joe. Mr. Wiggs, I enjoyed that last record of yours. I thought it was mighty fine. Thank you. How old are you, sir? I'm only 70. Only 70? I'm a stripling. Uh-huh. Well, Joe claims I'm over 100, so I... Oh, get away now. Outdate you. Not with that voice. Not with that voice. You're not anywhere near. Anyway, I've never heard anybody explain how jazz originally originated. And as a boy, well, I say that jazz first started for music songs that were sung by the field hands. I used to listen to them.…
Well, it's supposed to have been from a French quadrille, originally, that is one story.
